q: Kubernetes(K8s) 解决的核心问题是什么？
q_en: What core problem does Kubernetes solve?
options: 编排一群容器：调度到哪台机器、崩了重启、按负载扩缩、分发流量
它和 Docker 一样，只是用来构建和打包单个容器镜像的工具
它是一个专门用来集中存储容器运行日志的时序数据库
它是一种比容器隔离更强、每个应用独享内核的新型虚拟机
options_en: Orchestrating many containers: scheduling them onto machines, restarting crashes, autoscaling with load, routing traffic
Like Docker, it just builds and packages a single container image
A time-series database dedicated to storing container logs
A new kind of VM with stronger isolation where each app gets its own kernel
optionExplanations: 对：容器一多、跨多机，就需要一个「大管家」管调度/自愈/扩缩/负载均衡，这就是 K8s。
错：造/跑单个容器是 Docker 的活；K8s 管的是一整群容器。
错：日志是另一套(如 EFK)；K8s 是编排，不是日志库。
错：K8s 编排的正是容器，不是新虚拟机；隔离仍是容器那套。
optionExplanations_en: Right: once you have many containers across machines, you need an orchestrator for scheduling/self-healing/scaling/LB — that is K8s.
Wrong: building/running a single container is Docker; K8s manages a whole fleet.
Wrong: logging is a separate stack (e.g. EFK); K8s is orchestration, not a log store.
Wrong: K8s orchestrates containers, not a new VM; isolation is still the container model.
why: Docker 造/跑单个容器；容器一多、跨多台机器，就需要一个「大管家」决定调度、崩了自愈、按负载扩缩、分发流量——这就是 Kubernetes(编排)。
why_en: Docker builds and runs a single container; once you have many across machines you need an orchestrator for scheduling, self-healing, autoscaling, and load balancing — that is Kubernetes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 自动管理一群容器的部署、调度、扩缩、自愈、联网——K8s 干的事
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Orchestration is automatically deploying, scheduling, scaling, self-healing, and networking a fleet of containers.

termDefinitions.meaning: K8s 的「大脑」：API Server + scheduler + controller，决定期望状态并驱动集群向它收敛
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The control plane is K8s's brain (API server + scheduler + controllers) that drives the cluster toward the desired state.

q: K8s 里的 Pod 和 container 是一回事吗？
q_en: Are a Pod and a container the same thing in K8s?
options: 不是：Pod 是 K8s 最小调度单位，里面装 1 个或少数共享网络/存储的容器
是的，Pod 只是 container 的另一个名字，两者完全等价没有区别
Pod 是一台物理机，container 是跑在这台物理机上的虚拟机
一个 Pod 必须正好装 100 个 container，否则无法被调度运行
options_en: No: a Pod is the smallest K8s scheduling unit, wrapping one or a few containers that share network/storage
Yes, Pod is just another name for container — completely equivalent
A Pod is a physical machine and a container is a VM running on it
A Pod must contain exactly 100 containers or it cannot be scheduled
optionExplanations: 对：Pod 是 container 外面的一层包装，是 K8s 调度/扩缩的最小单位；常见 1 Pod=1 container。
错：Pod 能装多个共享 localhost 和卷的容器(如 sidecar)，不等于单个 container。
错：跑 Pod 的机器叫 Node；Pod/container 都不是物理机。
错：一个 Pod 通常 1 个容器，数量没有硬性规定，更不是 100。
optionExplanations_en: Right: a Pod wraps container(s) and is the smallest schedulable unit; commonly one Pod = one container.
Wrong: a Pod can hold several containers sharing localhost and volumes (e.g. a sidecar), so it is not just one container.
Wrong: the machine running Pods is a Node; neither Pod nor container is a physical machine.
Wrong: a Pod usually holds one container; there is no fixed count, certainly not 100.
why: Pod 是 K8s 调度/扩缩的最小单位，是 container 外面的一层包装：常见 1 Pod=1 container，但也能装几个紧耦合、共享 localhost 网络和卷的容器(如 sidecar)。扩容 = 加/减 Pod。
why_en: A Pod is the smallest schedulable unit — a wrapper around container(s). Usually one Pod = one container, but it can hold a few tightly-coupled containers sharing localhost and volumes (e.g. a sidecar). Scaling means adding/removing Pods.
tradeoff: container（运行时单位） vs Pod（K8s 调度单位，可含多个共享网络/卷的容器）

rows: 同 Pod 内共享网络/卷

termDefinitions.meaning: 和主容器同一个 Pod 里的辅助容器(如日志/代理)，共享网络和卷、随主容器一起调度
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sidecar is a helper container in the same Pod (e.g. logging/proxy) sharing its network and volumes.

q: 补全 K8s 的三个核心对象：
q_en: Fill in the three core Kubernetes objects:
text: K8s 里：{{Node}} 是一台机器(上面跑 Pod)；{{Deployment}} 声明「我要 N 个副本一直跑着」，崩了自动补；{{Service}} 是一组 Pod 前面的稳定地址 + 负载均衡。
text_en: In K8s: a {{Node}} is a machine that runs Pods; a {{Deployment}} declares "keep N replicas running" and self-heals; a {{Service}} is a stable address + load balancer in front of a set of Pods.
why: Node=机器、Pod=最小单位、Deployment=维持副本数(自愈)、Service=稳定入口+负载均衡。Pod 是会生灭的，Service 给它们一个不变的地址。
why_en: Node = machine, Pod = smallest unit, Deployment = keep N replicas (self-heal), Service = stable entry + load balancer. Pods come and go; a Service gives them one steady address.

termDefinitions.meaning: 声明式管理一组 Pod：维持副本数、崩了重建、支持滚动更新/回滚
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Deployment declaratively manages a set of Pods — keeps the replica count, recreates crashes, and does rolling updates/rollbacks.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一组 Pod 前的稳定虚拟地址 + 负载均衡；Pod 会换，Service 地址不变
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Service is a stable virtual address + load balancer in front of Pods; Pods change, the Service address stays.

scenario: 判题服务白天平峰、赛事时提交暴涨，想让副本数随 CPU 自动增减。
scenario_en: The judge service is flat by day but spikes during contests; you want replica count to rise and fall with CPU automatically.
q: 该用 K8s 的什么机制？
q_en: Which K8s mechanism should you use?
options: HPA：按 CPU / 指标自动增减 Pod 副本数（需 Metrics Server）
每次都手动 kubectl scale 改副本数，靠人盯着流量调整
Cluster Autoscaler，它的作用是按 CPU 增减 Pod 副本数
直接把这个服务换成 CPU 更多的大实例（垂直扩容）
options_en: HPA: automatically scale Pod replicas by CPU/metrics (needs Metrics Server)
Manually run kubectl scale each time, watching traffic by hand
Cluster Autoscaler, which scales Pod replicas by CPU
Just move the service to a bigger instance with more CPU (vertical scaling)
optionExplanations: 对：HPA 监控 Pod 的 CPU/指标，超阈值加 Pod、回落减 Pod，正是「突发自动扩」。
错：手动 scale 不能自动跟随突发，人也盯不过来。
错：Cluster Autoscaler 加的是 Node(机器)，不是 Pod 副本。
错：垂直扩容有 CPU 上限、不弹性、还烧空闲成本(见 leetcode-036)。
optionExplanations_en: Right: the HPA watches Pod CPU/metrics and adds/removes Pods above/below a target — exactly bursty autoscaling.
Wrong: manual scale cannot follow spikes automatically and no one can watch it continuously.
Wrong: the Cluster Autoscaler adds Nodes (machines), not Pod replicas.
Wrong: vertical scaling hits a CPU ceiling, is not elastic, and wastes idle cost (see leetcode-036).
why: HPA 监控 Pod 的 CPU/自定义指标，超阈值(如 50%)就加 Pod、回落就减；需要 Metrics Server 提供指标。这就是「判题突发自动扩 worker」的落地。
why_en: The HPA watches Pod CPU/custom metrics and adds Pods above a target (e.g. 50%), removing them when load drops; it needs a Metrics Server. This is how bursty judge autoscaling is implemented.
whenOtherWins: 若瓶颈不是副本数而是集群没机器了，该配合 Cluster Autoscaler 加 Node；若单请求就要更大内存/CPU，才考虑 VPA/垂直。
codeSample:
# 命令式：给 deployment judge 建 HPA，目标 CPU 50%，副本 2~10
kubectl autoscale deployment judge --cpu-percent=50 --min=2 --max=10
kubectl get hpa                 # 看当前副本数 / 指标

# 声明式 YAML (autoscaling/v2)：
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
spec:
  scaleTargetRef: { kind: Deployment, name: judge }
  minReplicas: 2
  maxReplicas: 10
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource: { name: cpu, target: { type: Utilization, averageUtilization: 50 } }

termDefinitions.meaning: K8s 组件：按 CPU/指标自动增减 Pod 副本数，让副本跟随负载
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The HPA automatically scales a workload's Pod replica count by CPU/metrics to match load.

termDefinitions.meaning: 采集各 Pod 的 CPU/内存指标并通过 K8s API 暴露；HPA 的前置依赖
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Metrics Server collects per-Pod CPU/memory and exposes it via the K8s API — a prerequisite for the HPA.

scenario: HPA 想再加 Pod，但集群现有机器的资源已经装不下新 Pod 了。
scenario_en: The HPA wants more Pods, but the current machines have no room to schedule them.
options: Cluster Autoscaler：Pod 调度不了时自动加 Node
HPA 会顺带把机器也一起加上，完全不需要别的组件配合
没办法自动，只能人工登录云控制台一台台手动加机器
K8s 会自动把现有机器的 CPU 变多，也就是垂直扩容机器
options_en: The Cluster Autoscaler: it sees unschedulable Pods and adds Nodes
The HPA also adds machines by itself, no other component needed
Nothing — you must log into the cloud console and add machines by hand
K8s automatically gives existing machines more CPU (vertical scaling)
optionExplanations: 对：它盯的是「有没有 Pod 被资源不足卡住」，被卡住就加机器、空了就撤。
错：HPA 只管 Pod 副本数，不碰机器数量。
错：手动加机器慢且不弹性，正是 CA 要自动化的事。
错：那是垂直扩容单机，不是 K8s 加机器的方式；也有上限。
optionExplanations_en: Right: the CA scans every ~10s for unschedulable Pods and adds Nodes, scaling Nodes back down when idle.
Wrong: the HPA only manages Pod replicas, not machine count.
Wrong: adding machines by hand is slow and inelastic — exactly what the CA automates.
Wrong: that is vertical scaling of one machine, not how K8s adds machines, and it has a ceiling.
why: HPA 加的是 Pod、Cluster Autoscaler 加的是 Node。CA 每约 10 秒检查有没有「因资源不足调度不了的 Pod」，有就加机器、空闲就缩机器。两者配合：HPA 加 Pod → 装不下 → CA 加 Node。
why_en: The HPA adds Pods; the Cluster Autoscaler adds Nodes. Every ~10s the CA checks for Pods that cannot be scheduled due to lack of resources and adds machines (removing idle ones). Together: HPA adds Pods → no room → CA adds Nodes.
whenOtherWins: 如果集群机器一直够用，只靠 HPA 就行，不必开 CA；固定容量、成本敏感时也可不开 CA。

termDefinitions.meaning: 按「有没有调度不了的 Pod」自动加/减 Node(机器)；每约 10 秒检查一次
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Cluster Autoscaler adds/removes Nodes based on whether Pods are unschedulable, checking about every 10s.

termDefinitions.meaning: 因当前集群资源(CPU/内存)不足而无法被放到任何 Node 上的 Pod
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An unschedulable Pod is one that cannot be placed on any Node because the cluster lacks the CPU/memory it requests.

tradeoff: HPA（扩 Pod·按指标） vs Cluster Autoscaler（扩 Node·按调度失败）

q: HPA 和 Cluster Autoscaler 的区别与配合是什么？
q_en: How do the HPA and Cluster Autoscaler differ and work together?
options: HPA 按指标加/减 Pod 副本；CA 按「Pod 调度不了」加/减 Node；HPA 加 Pod 装不下就触发 CA 加机器
两者完全一样，只是新旧版本不同的名字而已
HPA 加机器，Cluster Autoscaler 加 Pod，正好相反
两者都只能手动触发，不能根据负载自动运行
options_en: The HPA scales Pod replicas by metrics; the CA scales Nodes when Pods cannot schedule; HPA adding Pods that do not fit triggers the CA to add machines
They are identical, just old and new names for the same thing
The HPA adds machines and the Cluster Autoscaler adds Pods — the opposite
Both can only be triggered manually and never run automatically by load
optionExplanations: 对：一个管 Pod 数、一个管 Node 数，方向不同但互补，串起来实现端到端弹性。
错：一个扩 Pod、一个扩 Node，机制和触发都不同，不是一回事。
错：说反了——HPA 扩 Pod，CA 扩 Node。
错：两者都是按负载/调度状态自动运行，不是手动。
optionExplanations_en: Right: one scales Pods, one scales Nodes — different but complementary, giving end-to-end elasticity.
Wrong: one scales Pods, the other Nodes, with different triggers — not the same.
Wrong: reversed — the HPA scales Pods, the CA scales Nodes.
Wrong: both run automatically from load/scheduling state, not manually.
why: HPA 扩的是 Pod(按 CPU/指标)，Cluster Autoscaler 扩的是 Node(按有没有调度不了的 Pod)。它们互补：HPA 先加 Pod，集群装不下时 CA 再加机器；负载回落时反向缩。
why_en: The HPA scales Pods (by CPU/metrics); the Cluster Autoscaler scales Nodes (by whether Pods are unschedulable). They complement: HPA adds Pods first, and when the cluster is full the CA adds machines; both scale back down as load falls.
tradeoff: HPA（扩 Pod·按指标·需 Metrics Server） vs Cluster Autoscaler（扩 Node·按调度失败·依赖云 node pool）

scenario: 一个小规模内部工具，就几个服务、流量也不大。
scenario_en: A small internal tool with a handful of services and modest traffic.
q: 什么时候才值得上 Kubernetes？
q_en: When is Kubernetes actually worth it?
options: 很多容器/服务、跨多机、要自愈+弹性扩缩+滚动发布时；小规模上 K8s 是过度设计
任何项目从第一天起都应该先搭一套 K8s 再写业务
K8s 只有超大公司能用，中小团队一律不能碰
K8s 能替代写业务代码，上了它就不用自己实现功能了
options_en: When you have many containers/services across machines needing self-healing, elastic scaling, and rolling deploys; at small scale K8s is over-engineering
Every project should stand up K8s on day one before writing any business logic
Only huge companies can use K8s; small teams must never touch it
K8s replaces writing business code — once you have it you need not implement features
optionExplanations: 对：K8s 的价值在「多容器跨多机的编排+弹性+自愈」；东西少时它的复杂度大于收益。
错：第一天就上 K8s 是典型过早复杂化，小系统单体/几个容器就够(见 leetcode-010)。
错：托管 K8s(EKS/GKE)让中小团队也能用，不是大厂专属。
错：K8s 只管运行/编排，不写你的业务逻辑。
optionExplanations_en: Right: K8s pays off for orchestration + elasticity + self-healing across many containers and machines; at small scale its complexity outweighs the benefit.
Wrong: K8s on day one is premature complexity; a small system needs a monolith or a few containers (see leetcode-010).
Wrong: managed K8s (EKS/GKE) makes it accessible to small teams too, not just giants.
Wrong: K8s only runs/orchestrates; it does not write your business logic.
why: K8s 的价值是「很多容器、跨多机」时的编排、弹性伸缩、自愈、滚动发布。东西少、流量小的时候，它的运维复杂度 > 收益——那就单体或几个容器 + 简单编排即可，别过度设计。
why_en: K8s pays off when you orchestrate many containers across many machines with elastic scaling, self-healing, and rolling deploys. At small scale its operational complexity outweighs the benefit — a monolith or a few containers is enough; do not over-engineer.
whenOtherWins: 规模一旦上来(几十个服务、要弹性和滚动发布、多团队)，K8s 的编排价值就压过它的复杂度。

termDefinitions.meaning: 云厂商托管的 K8s(EKS/GKE/AKS)，省去自己维护 control plane，中小团队也能用
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Managed Kubernetes (EKS/GKE/AKS) is cloud-run K8s that removes control-plane maintenance, making it accessible to small teams.
